editorial:
Imagine stumbling upon a weird, indie project that feels like a fever dream. You get dropped into a world where the rules are blurry and the characters feel like they are just winging it. It has a gritty, low-budget energy that makes you feel like you are watching something you weren't supposed to find. The vibe is totally chaotic, mixing drama with a strange sense of humor that keeps you guessing about what is actually going on. It does not hold your hand, so you have to pay close attention to the small details to keep up with the story.

What really hits home is how raw the acting feels, even if it is a bit messy at times. The pacing is a bit uneven, but the surprising twists make up for the slow parts. If you enjoy movies that feel like a puzzle, you will love this. endingExplained: In the final act, you find out that the main character has been imagining his rival the entire time. Everything that happened was just a fight inside his own head to deal with stress. The movie ends with him finally accepting his true self and breaking down the walls he built. He stops fighting the imaginary person and decides to start his life over with a clear mind, leaving the chaos behind for good.
